from parse import parse_line
from clean import clean_title
from money import parse_salary
from rules import keep
from pipeline import run

# Test money parsing handling spaces as thousands separators
def test_money_parse_salary_space_separators():
    assert parse_salary('1 200 000') == 1200000
    assert parse_salary('50 000') == 50000

# Test rules keep includes salaries equal to minimum
def test_rules_keep_equality():
    jobs = [{'salary': 50000}]
    assert keep(jobs, 50000) == jobs

# Test pipeline run
def test_pipeline_run():
    lines = [
        '1;Senior Engineer;1 200 000',
        '2;Junior Developer;50 000',
        '3;Intern;30 000'
    ]
    results = run(lines, 50000)
    ids = [job['id'] for job in results]
    assert set(ids) == {'1', '2'}
    assert results[0]['title'] == 'Senior Engineer'
    assert results[1]['title'] == 'Junior Developer'
    assert all(isinstance(job['salary'], int) for job in results)
    assert all(job['salary'] >= 50000 for job in results)

# Test parse_line
def test_parse_line():
    line = '  99  ;   some title  ;  100 00 '
    job = parse_line(line)
    assert job['id'] == '99'
    assert job['salary'] == '100 00'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_money_parse_salary_space_separators()
    test_rules_keep_equality()
    test_pipeline_run()
    test_parse_line()
    print('All tests passed!')
